$comment: The framework/app ownership boundary. `npm run framework:verify` reads this file.
WHY THIS EXISTS: a portal built from this skeleton must be able to receive framework
updates forever. That only works if every file has exactly one owner, so no framework
update ever has to merge into a file an app also writes. See docs/DECISIONS.md.
WHERE FRAMEWORK FILES LIVE, and how each is delivered. Phase 2 moved the runtime code under
platform/ behind an @framework/* alias; phase 7 settled everything that could not move there:
Inside a subtree prefix (see the subtree block) — delivered by `framework:update`:
platform/**   the runtime code, scripts, config, and the materialized canonical copies
.claude/**    agent policy; Claude Code reads it from this hardcoded path, so it stays at
the project root and gets its own prefix rather than being duplicated
.agents/**    the same, for non-Claude agent tooling
Materialized — a canonical copy inside platform/materialized/, copied out by
`framework:apply`, because the real path is one no subtree prefix can cover:
root files a tool hardcodes (vite.config.ts, the tsconfigs, components.json, dotfiles,
src/main.tsx, src/vite-env.d.ts), the root docs (DESIGN.md, tailwind.md, ARCHITECTURE.md,
CONTRIBUTING.md, skills-lock.json), and the framework docs that sit in otherwise
app-owned directories (docs/architecture/*, docs/COMMANDS.md, docs/PREFLIGHT.md,
docs/wip/{README,_TEMPLATE}.md, docs/plan/{README,units/_TEMPLATE}.md).
THE INVARIANT phase 7 established: a file may only be hash-checked if one of those two
mechanisms can actually deliver it. Before that, 101 framework files were hash-checked with no
delivery path at all, so the first release touching any of them reported 'framework file
modified' in every portal — for files the portal had never edited.
See docs/DECISIONS.md for the full reasoning.
$roleNote: `role` is deliberately NOT in this file — it lives in package.json's `framework.role`.
This file is inside the git-subtree prefix (platform/), so `npm run framework:update`
overwrites it wholesale. A role stored here would be reset from "consumer" to "source" on
every update, silently disabling BOTH halves of Gate B — the lock hash-check in
framework-verify.mjs and the .claude/hooks/guard-framework.mjs block — because each keys off
that single field. The portal would look protected and not be.
package.json is `seeded`: written once by app:init, app-owned, never synced. That makes it
the only correct home for a per-repo setting. See platform/scripts/framework-lib.mjs's

$comment: How this framework is published and pulled back. Each entry is one `git subtree` prefix
published to its own BRANCH of the same framework repo — `git subtree split --prefix=X`
produces a history whose root is X's contents, which is why the framework repo has no
platform/ directory of its own.
WHY THREE PREFIXES, not one: subtree can only ever see the single directory named by its
prefix. Files outside it are invisible to push/pull. `.claude/**` and `.agents/**` are
framework-owned but sit at the project root (Claude Code and other agent tooling read them
from hardcoded paths), so with only the platform/ prefix they were hash-checked against a
lock they could never match after any release — a false 'framework file modified' on every
portal. Giving each its own prefix delivers them properly instead. See docs/DECISIONS.md.
`.claude/` is a MIXED directory — the framework's 19 skills plus any skill a portal adds —
and that is safe: `subtree pull` MERGES, so upstream changing build-datatable and a portal
having added acme-billing/ both survive, on every future pull. App skills classify `app`
(see ownership.app) so they are never hash-checked.
Framework files that are NOT inside any prefix — root files like DESIGN.md, and the
framework docs in directories that are otherwise app-owned — are `materialized` instead:
a canonical copy inside platform/ that framework:apply copies out. docs/architecture/ was
considered as a 4th prefix and rejected; see the materialized block's note.
`remote` is null until the real Gitea/GitHub repo exists. framework:publish, :update and
:link all refuse to run while it is null rather than guessing a URL — set it once and every
command works. A local bare repo path is a valid value, which is how the round trip was
proven before any host existed.
Classification is FIRST MATCH WINS, in the order the categories appear below.
That is what would let one specific file be framework while its whole directory is app —
the mechanism `src/services/auth.ts` (now `platform/src/services/auth.ts`) used to need.
ignored      — not owned by anyone; build output, local-only, tool scratch
framework    — replaced from upstream on update; hand-edits rejected in a consumer repo
materialized — framework content that must sit at a fixed path tooling expects, so it is
copied there by `framework:apply` and hash-checked like framework files
seeded       — written once by `app:init`, then belongs to the app and is never synced
app          — authored by the app; the framework never reads or writes it
Anything matching none of these is UNCLASSIFIED and verify reports it. That is the
point of this file: a new file with no declared owner is the failure mode to catch.
Two classifications that are not obvious from the path:
.agents/** is framework — it holds a second copy of the vendored upstream shadcn and
migrate-radix-to-base skills that also live under .claude/skills/ (not symlinks; real
duplicates, both hash-tracked by skills-lock.json).
src/integrations/supabase/types.ts is app — it is generated per portal from that
portal's own database by `npm run gen-supabase-types`, so the framework must not
depend on it (see the client.ts seam in phase 1).
PHASE 5 CORRECTIONS — four paths were classified framework that a portal must be able to
write, which made each of them read-only downstream and blocked the portal from operating:
docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/OWNERS.md  -> seeded  (see the seeded block's own note)
docs/architecture/inventory.md     -> app     (GENERATED per repo by `npm run docs:arch`
from that repo's own routes/services/pages, so its content necessarily differs in
every portal. CI runs `docs:arch -- --check`, so a portal MUST regenerate it — which
Gate B would then have rejected. guard-generated.mjs already blocks hand-editing it.)
.claude/skills/**                  -> app for anything not one of the framework's own 19
skills, which are now listed individually. The old blanket glob meant a portal adding
its own skill saw it reported as an unexpected new framework file.
Anything else a portal adds under docs/architecture/ falls through to app for the same
reason; the framework's own area docs are enumerated explicitly.
Framework content at a path the toolchain hardcodes, so it cannot live under
platform/. `framework:apply` copies it out and verify hash-checks it in place.
Editing one of these in an app repo is rejected exactly like a framework file —
change it upstream instead.
vite.config.ts and the tsconfigs carry the @framework alias, so an app that edits
them breaks the boundary itself. If a portal ever genuinely needs an extra Vite
plugin, that is an extension seam to design upstream, not a local edit.
src/main.tsx and src/vite-env.d.ts joined this category in phase 2 — see the
PHASE NOTE above the ownership block for why they didn't move to platform/ instead.
PHASE 7 added the second group below: framework docs and root files that are not inside
ANY subtree prefix. Root files can never be a prefix (a prefix is a directory), and
docs/wip/ + docs/plan/ are otherwise app-owned, so only their framework files are listed.
docs/architecture/ WAS considered as a 4th subtree prefix and deliberately rejected: it is
a directory, and the same merge logic that makes a mixed .claude/ safe would work — but it
would only save the 9 architecture docs (DESIGN.md is a root file, so materialized either
way) at the cost of a 4th `subtree split`+push on every publish and pull on every update,
and split walks the whole history. Don't 'improve' this into four prefixes without
re-reading this note.
Cost of this group: ~20 duplicated files, DESIGN.md (41 KB) and tailwind.md (24 KB
) included, so an edit to either shows twice in a diff. The trade buys something phase 1
explicitly gave up: framework *spec* improvements now reach existing portals.
`framework:apply -- --check` in CI stops the two copies drifting.
Written once by `app:init`, then the app's forever. A framework improvement to one
of these does NOT reach existing portals — that is the accepted trade for files
every portal must be free to rewrite.
home.routes.tsx is seeded rather than framework because it imports Home.tsx, which
the app owns; a framework file may never import app code.
docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/OWNERS.md are seeded, NOT framework. They ship with content
(the framework's own decision history and an owners template) but a portal has to be able
to append its own decisions and name its own team — DECISIONS.md is append-only by its own
header. Classifying them framework made both read-only downstream, which would have made a
portal unable to record why it did anything. app:init should reset DECISIONS.md rather than
leaving a portal inheriting 40 entries about framework internals.
public/config/app.json is seeded, NOT ignored. It was classified ignored while .gitignore
also listed it — but the file is, and must be, TRACKED: appConfig fetches /config/app.json
at startup and Vite copies public/ into dist/, so untracking it leaves the built image with
no config and appConfig.initialize() fails at boot. It is deployment config a portal owns
after app:init stamps it, which is exactly what seeded means. Only the publishable (anon)
key ever belongs in it — it is served over HTTP from public/.
What framework code imports. An app repo owns package.json, so verify does not edit
it — it reports the exact `npm i` line when one of these is missing or out of range.
Anything an app adds for itself is none of the framework's business.
Postgres schemas `npm run gen-supabase-types` must ALWAYS pass to the CLI, whatever else a
portal adds. These are the framework's own: dropping one strips its tables from the shared
`Database` type and every framework service silently loses its typing.
appContracts' mustContain markers are the after-the-fact check for the same thing. This list
is the before-the-fact one, and gen-supabase-types.mjs asserts the two agree, so they cannot
drift into disagreeing about what the framework needs.
A portal's OWN schemas do not belong here — they go in package.json's `supabase.schemas`,
which is app-owned. That split is the point: a portal can add schemas freely and can never
remove the framework's. `_common`, `_content` and `_training` were in the hardcoded list
before this existed and are deliberately NOT here: no source file references them, and a
portal whose database lacks them had the command fail outright (docs/GUIDE.md's failure #3).
Files the APP must provide because the FRAMEWORK depends on them. This inverts the normal
direction, so the list is deliberately tiny and each entry has to justify itself.
Why this is legitimate rather than a leak: a generated schema description is not app
behaviour. `npm run gen-supabase-types` emits ONE `Database` type covering the framework's
schemas (_arch, _secure) and the app's (public) together, and client.ts exports a single
`supabase` proxy typed by it. Whichever Database parameterises that client is what every
consumer sees — so the framework hand-declaring its own would strip the app's tables from
the shared client and break every app service. One shared contract is the correct shape.
verify asserts the file exists and still contains the schemas the framework's services
query, so a portal that regenerates types with a narrower --schema list fails loudly here
instead of at runtime.

knownGaps: No migrations create the _arch / _secure / _common schemas the nav, auth and user services query. A fresh Supabase project cannot run this skeleton; portals must point at a project that already has them. The table shapes are readable from src/integrations/supabase/types.ts.
